function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is essentially a formal instruction or authorization that gives someone (usually a financial institution or service provider) the right to act on behalf of another party. Think of it as a “give‑me‑permission” document that tells the institution what it can do and under what conditions. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Allows a third party (e.g., a bank, investment platform, or payment service) to perform specific actions—like making payments, managing investments, or executing trades—on your behalf. | | **Typical content** | • The identity of the authorized party
• The scope of authority (e.g., “pay monthly rent,” “manage my portfolio”)
• Time limits or conditions (e.g., “effective until 31 Dec 2025”)
• Any restrictions or special instructions | | **Status categories** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer in force. | ### Common examples | Scenario | How a mandate works | |----------|---------------------| | **Direct debit** | You give your bank a mandate to pull a fixed amount from your account each month to pay a utility bill. | | **Investment management** | An investment firm receives a mandate to buy/sell securities on your behalf according to a set strategy. | | **Payment services** | A merchant’s payment processor gets a mandate to settle funds into the merchant’s account after a transaction. | ### Why it matters - **Legal clarity** – The mandate defines who can act and how, reducing disputes. - **Security** – Only authorized parties can access your funds or data. - **Automation** – Once a mandate is in place, routine tasks (like recurring payments) can run automatically without manual intervention. In short, a mandate is the official “permission slip” that lets a trusted partner manage certain financial activities for you.
